sources: Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran' (cross-check)
Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)

defacto.controller: Soviet Union (44th and 47th Armies)
defacto.note: Soviet troops took Tabriz and Ardabil by 26 Aug 1941. Iranian civil administration continued; the Tripartite Treaty (29 Jan 1942) declared the presence not an occupation and required withdrawal within six months of the end of hostilities (2 March 1946).
sources: Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)

defacto.controller: Azerbaijan People's Government (Democratic Party of Azerbaijan; Ja'far Pishevari, premier) under Soviet protection
defacto.note: The Democrats took Tabriz around 20-21 Nov 1945 and proclaimed the Autonomous Government of Azerbaijan on 12 Dec 1945 while Soviet troops blocked the Iranian army. Soviet forces left in May 1946; Iranian forces began moving in on 9 Dec 1946 and entered Tabriz on 12-13 Dec 1946, when Pishevari fled to Baku.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)
Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)

defacto.controller: Soviet Union (based at Mashhad and Bojnurd)
defacto.note: Soviet troops entered Khorasan on 3 Shahrivar 1320 (25 Aug 1941) from Sarakhs, Dargaz and Bajgiran and, per Iranica, "occupied all of Khorasan until the winter of 1943". After that Soviet presence there was withdrawn (the exact month is not given).
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

defacto.controller: Soviet Union
defacto.note: Soviet forces took Gilan (Anzali, Rasht), Mazandaran and Gorgan in August 1941 and reached Qazvin; they entered Tehran on 17 Sept 1941 and withdrew from it by 17 Oct. Iranian civil administration continued. The last Soviet troops left on about 6-9 May 1946.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)
Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)

events.title: Qajar-era lease of Bandar Abbas and the Minab-Khamir coast to Muscat
events.summary: Under a Persian firman of 1793 (lease of 1794) the Sultan of Muscat administered Bandar Abbas, the coast from Minab to Khamir and the islands of Qeshm and Hormuz for 75 years. The arrangement was contested in 1804-10 by Mulla Hosein of Qeshm and the Qawasim and was restricted to 20 years from 1855.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bandar-e ʿAbbās i. The City' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bandar-e-abbasi/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qešm Island' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qeshm-island/)
Qatar Digital Library, 'No Place Equal to It: The Omani Lease of Bandar Abbas' parts 1-2 (qdl.qa) [search extract]

events.title: Qajars retake Mashhad from Nader Mirza Afshar
events.summary: After failed attempts in 1799 and 1801 and a personal campaign in 1802, Fath-Ali Shah's forces under Mohammad-Vali Mirza entered Mashhad in early 1803. Nader Mirza was taken to Tehran and executed; Khorasan came under Qajar control, though local khans kept wide autonomy.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fath-'Ali Shah Qajar' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fath-ali-shah-qajar-2/) [search extract]
Wikipedia, 'Nader Mirza Afshar' (cross-check only)

events.title: Russian army occupies Tabriz, Urmia and Ardabil
events.summary: Paskevich took Tabriz (13 Oct 1827), Urmia (28 Jan 1828) and Ardabil (8 Feb 1828). Under Turkmenchay (22 Feb 1828) Russia kept Azerbaijan as security for the 10-kurur indemnity and withdrew by stages (Tabriz in March; Khoy and neighbours after instalments). Final evacuation date unverified.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Treaty of Turkmenchay' and 'Russo-Persian War (1826-1828)' (cross-check; Tabriz 13 Oct 1827, Urmia 28 Jan 1828, Ardabil 8 Feb 1828)
Qatar Digital Library, 'Enclosure no 1 to letter of 16 Mar 1828' (qdl.qa) [search extract: Paskevich leaving Tabriz, evacuation of Khoy tied to indemnity instalments]

events.title: Abbas Mirza captures Mohammad Khan Qara'i; end of the Qara'i principality
events.summary: Crown Prince Abbas Mirza took Mohammad Khan Qara'i of Torbat-e Heydarieh by deception in 1832; Qajar appointees governed Torbat thereafter.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Mohammad Khan Qaraei-Torbati' (cross-check; rule 1816-32, capture 1832)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Esḥāq Khan Qarāʾī' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/eshaq-qarai/) [search extract]

events.title: Ottoman capture of Muhammara by Ali Rida Pasha
events.summary: The Ottoman governor of Baghdad invaded the Ka'b sheikhdom of Muhammara, captured and destroyed the town and received the sheikhs' homage; the town was then alternately claimed and held by Persia and the Ottomans until 1847. How long the Ottoman occupation lasted in 1837 is not established.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ali Rıza Pasha (governor of Baghdad)' (cross-check; 1837 capture of Muhammara)
Wikipedia, 'Khorramshahr' (cross-check; alternately claimed and occupied by Persia and Turkey until the 1847 Treaty of Erzurum)

events.title: British occupation of Kharg Island (first)
events.summary: Britain occupied Kharg on 19 June 1838 as a response to Mohammad Shah's siege of Herat and moved its Residency there from Bushehr. The island was held until March 1842 because of Persian diplomatic evasions.
sources: Qatar Digital Library, 'A Strategic Position: British Seizures of the Island of Kharg' and Lorimer, Gazetteer (occupation 19 June 1838 - March 1842) [search extracts]

events.title: Russia founds a naval station on Ashurada
events.summary: After a 1838 Persian request for help against Turkmen raiders, Russia built barracks and stationed warships on Ashurada in Gorgan Bay; Iranica says the station existed by 1842 (other dates: 1837, 1841). Russia recognised Persian sovereignty but refused to leave until the 1921 Persian-Soviet treaty.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Āšūrāda' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/asurada/)
Wikipedia, 'Ashuradeh' (cross-check; 1837 / 1841 variants)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Gorgān vii. History from the Safavids to the end of the Pahlavi era' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/gorgan-vii/)

events.title: Second Treaty of Erzurum cedes Mohammerah to Persia
events.summary: Article II of the treaty ceded the town and port of Mohammerah, its anchorage within the Haffar canal and Khizr island to Persia, ending a period in which Muhammara had been alternately claimed and occupied by Persians and Ottomans. (De jure effects are for the frontier layer.)
sources: Treaty of Erzurum, 31 May 1847, Article II (cession of Mohammerah town/port and Khizr island to Persia), as summarised in QDL 'Memorandum respecting the frontier between Mohammerah and Turkey' [search extract]
Wikipedia, 'Khorramshahr' (cross-check; alternately claimed and occupied by Persia and Turkey until the 1847 Treaty of Erzurum)

events.title: Mashhad rises for Hasan Khan Salar
events.summary: Mashhad's residents and ulama massacred officials and soldiers on 25 Aug 1848, just before Mohammad Shah's death, and Salar made the shrine city the centre of a revolt that had begun in northern Khorasan in 1846-47. Hamza Mirza's army withdrew and Salar dominated most of Khorasan.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Revolt of Hasan Khan Salar' (cross-check; the only source consulted giving the 1848-50 day-level chronology)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Persian troops occupy Bampur
events.summary: Persian forces occupied Bampur in 1849 and garrisoned it permanently in 1850; the local rulers of Dizzak, Sarbaz, Geh and Qasr-e Qand then accepted the obligation to pay taxes to the governor, Ebrahim Khan. Before this Persian Baluchistan was "practically independent".
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Baluchistan i. Geography, History and Ethnography' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/baluchistan-index/baluchistan-i/) [search extract]
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Kerman ix. History in the Qajar Period' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kerman-09-qajar-period/)

events.title: Mashhad surrenders; Hasan Khan Salar executed
events.summary: Sultan Morad Mirza retook Sabzevar (9 March 1849) and Neyshabur (21 March 1849) and besieged Mashhad from June 1849; the city surrendered on 13 or 23 March 1850 and Salar, his son and brother were executed on 29 April 1850.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Revolt of Hasan Khan Salar' (cross-check; the only source consulted giving the 1848-50 day-level chronology)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Anglo-Persian War: British take Kharg and Bushehr
events.summary: British naval forces occupied Kharg on 4 Dec 1856, stormed Reshire on 5 Dec and took Bushehr on 9-10 Dec 1856; Borazjan was occupied on 5 Feb 1857 and the Battle of Khushab was fought on 8 Feb.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Anglo-Persian War (1856-57)' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/anglo-persian-war-1856-57/)
Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Persian War' (cross-check; Bushehr evacuated Oct 1857)

events.title: British take Mohammerah and reach Ahvaz
events.summary: After a naval bombardment Mohammerah fell on 26-27 March 1857 and an armed flotilla reached Ahvaz on 1 April; the Treaty of Paris (signed 4 March, ratified 2 May 1857) ended the war.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Anglo-Persian War (1856-57)' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/anglo-persian-war-1856-57/)
Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Persian War' (cross-check; Bushehr evacuated Oct 1857)

events.title: British evacuate Mohammerah, Bushehr and Kharg
events.summary: The main British force left the Gulf in mid-1857 (May-June, because of the Indian Mutiny); Bushehr was evacuated in October 1857 (Wikipedia) and Kharg held until spring 1858 (Iranica). Exact dates by place are not firmly established.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Anglo-Persian War (1856-57)' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/anglo-persian-war-1856-57/)
Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Persian War' (cross-check; Bushehr evacuated Oct 1857)

events.title: Naser al-Din Shah abolishes the Ardalan vilayet
events.summary: In 1284/1867-68 the shah ended Kurdistan's special status as a semi-autonomous frontier province and appointed his uncle Farhad Mirza Mo'tamed al-Dowleh governor, ending Ardalan rule.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Banī Ardalān' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bani-ardalan-a-kurdish-tribe-of-northwestern-iran-now-dispersed-in-sanandaj-senna-and-surrounding-villages/) [search extract]
Wikipedia, 'Ardalan' (cross-check)

events.title: Persia regains Bandar Abbas from Muscat
events.summary: After the expulsion of Sayyid Salim bin Thuwaini from Muscat (October 1868) the lease became void; Persia appointed Haji Ahmad, formerly Salim's minister, to govern Bandar Abbas and its dependencies.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bandar-e ʿAbbās i. The City' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bandar-e-abbasi/)
Qatar Digital Library, 'No Place Equal to It: The Omani Lease of Bandar Abbas' parts 1-2 (qdl.qa) [search extract]

events.title: Persian forces expel an Omani claimant from Chahbar
events.summary: 'Abd al-'Aziz, brother of the Sultan of Muscat, seized Chahbar in January 1872; a Persian army expelled him in March (the governor of Bampur, Sartip Ebrahim Khan, had asserted Persian ownership), ending Oman's hold.
sources: Lorimer, Gazetteer of the Persian Gulf (1915), via Qatar Digital Library (qdl.qa), entry on Chahbar 1872 [search extract]

events.title: Goldsmid arbitration awards west Sistan to Persia
events.summary: The British arbitration mission under Col. Goldsmid divided Sistan: the lands west of the Helmand were awarded to Persia and the right bank to Afghanistan. Sistanis rebelled against the Qa'en chief later that year and Persian governors followed in 1873.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Helmand river iv' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/helmand-river-iv/) [search extract on 1872 Goldsmid award]
Qatar Digital Library, 'Military Report on Persian Seistan' and 'Seistan arbitration case' (British Library IOR; qdl.qa) [search extracts]

events.title: Sheikh Ubeydullah's invasion of north-west Persia
events.summary: In the last months of 1880 tens of thousands of Ottoman and Iranian Kurds under Sheikh Ubeydullah of Nehri took control of Sauj Bulaq and Maragheh and ravaged villages around Urmia; Urmia held out and the host withdrew after about eight weeks.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Uprising of Sheikh Ubeydullah' (cross-check; ~8 weeks, Mahabad and Maragheh taken, Urmia held out)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, extract on Sheikh Ubeydullah's 1298/1880 invasion of Azarbaijan (iranicaonline.org, 'Kurdish language ii' / 'Safavid dynasty (cont.)' search results)

events.title: Akhal-Khorasan convention fixes the Russo-Persian frontier in the Turkmen steppe
events.summary: Following the Russian conquest of the Akhal Teke, the 1299/1881 convention effectively ended Iran's claims to Marv and the Turkmen steppe; the Yomut and Goklen within Persia thereafter dealt with a Russian-bordered Persian state. (Frontier effects are for the frontier layer.)
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Persia ends Qasimi rule at Bandar Lengeh
events.summary: In February 1887 Persia created the "Gulf Ports" governorate (Bushehr, Lengeh, Bandar Abbas); in September the Qasimi governorship of Lengeh was dissolved, Sheikh Qazib was arrested and sent to Tehran and a Persian garrison landed. A 1898-99 interlude under Sheikh Mohammad ibn Khalifa ended when Ahmad Khan Daryabeigi retook the town in March 1899.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Bandar-e Lenga' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/bandar-e-lenga/) and 'Great Britain iii'/'Abu Musa' search extracts on 1887
Wikipedia, 'Bandar Lengeh' (cross-check; 1887-88 takeover, 1898-99 interlude)

events.title: Khaz'al becomes Sheikh of Mohammerah
events.summary: Khaz'al Khan succeeded his assassinated brother Mazal as sheikh of Mohammerah in June 1897 and built a semi-independent realm in Khuzestan under British protection.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Ḵazʿal Khan' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kazal-khan/)

events.title: Ottoman troops occupy Persian frontier districts
events.summary: Beginning 23 May 1906 at Behik in Baradost, Ottoman troops occupied Dasht, Mergever, Sardasht and other districts from south-west of Sauj Bulaq to west of Khoy, collected taxes near Urmia and re-occupied Mergever on 3 Aug 1907. Russian and British pressure and a frontier commission pushed them back around 1911-12.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Ottoman invasion of Persia (1906)' (cross-check; 23 May 1906 onward)
Qatar Digital Library, India Office file 'Turco-Persian Frontier' 1912 (qdl.qa) [search extract]

events.title: Tabriz resists Mohammad Ali Shah's coup
events.summary: Constitutionalists led by Sattar Khan and Baqer Khan held Tabriz against a royalist siege from the shah's coup (23 June 1908) until Russian troops entered on 30 April 1909.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Russian occupation of Tabriz' (23 June 1908 rebellion date; cross-check)

events.title: Constitutionalists seize Rasht and Isfahan
events.summary: In January 1909 constitutionalist forces took Rasht and Bakhtiari khans took Isfahan; columns from Gilan and Isfahan then marched on Tehran. Months are approximate.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Russia i. Russo-Iranian Relations up to the Bolshevik Revolution' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/russia-i-relations/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Baḵtīārī' articles incl. 'Baḵtīārī tribe', 'Esfandīār Khan', 'Baktiari ii' (iranicaonline.org) [search extracts]

events.title: Sayyed Abd al-Hosayn Lari's revolt in Larestan
events.summary: A pro-constitution mujtahid proclaimed a revolt in 1909, issued his own stamps and, per Iranica, ruled Larestan until spring 1915, when Qavam al-Molk's force sent by the governor-general of Fars pacified it. Continuity of control between 1909 and 1915 is uncertain.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv' (Sayyed ʿAbd-al-Ḥosayn Lārī 1909-spring 1915) [search extract]
Lorimer-based extract quoted by philatelic sources: Lari's stamps in use March-May 1909; re-entered Lar August 1909 (rpsl.org.uk / qdl.qa 'Administration Reports 1905-10') [search extract]

events.title: Russian troops occupy Tabriz (and land at Anzali)
events.summary: On 20 April 1909 Britain, France and Russia agreed to Russian intervention; Gen. Snarski's force occupied Tabriz on 30 April 1909 and Russian troops landed at Anzali and advanced on Qazvin. Russia kept troops in Tabriz, Gilan and Khorasan to 1918.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Russian occupation of Tabriz' (cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Russia i. Russo-Iranian Relations up to the Bolshevik Revolution' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/russia-i-relations/)

events.title: Constitutionalist forces take Tehran
events.summary: Gilani and Bakhtiari columns took Tehran on 13 July 1909 and deposed Mohammad Ali Shah, ending the rebel-held phases at Rasht and Isfahan.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Russia i. Russo-Iranian Relations up to the Bolshevik Revolution' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/russia-i-relations/)

events.title: Salar al-Dowleh's revolt in the west
events.summary: After Mohammad Ali Shah's return attempt, his brother occupied Sanandaj by 17 July 1911 and took Kermanshah and Hamadan with tribal levies; he was beaten at Saveh by Amir Mofakham Bakhtiari and the revolt was finally quelled in 1912-13 (Farmanfarma). A first revolt in 1907 was routed at Nehavand (Iranica). Mohammad Ali Shah's own July 1911 landing near Astarabad was defeated within weeks and is not mapped (not independently verified here). Duration of control of each town is not established.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Kermanshah iv. History to 1953' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kermanshah-04-history-to-1953/)
Not independently verified in this research pass; reconstructed from general scholarship

events.title: Ottoman forces briefly take Urmia and Tabriz
events.summary: Ottoman volunteers took Urmia on 4 Jan 1915 and Kurdish/Ottoman troops entered Tabriz on 8 Jan after the Russian evacuation (17 Dec 1914); Russia re-entered Tabriz on 31 Jan 1915. Under a month, so no region record.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Russian occupation of Tabriz' (cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915)
Wikipedia, 'Persian campaign (World War I)' (cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations)

events.title: British East Persia Cordon is formed
events.summary: In July 1915 a small force on the Baluchistan frontier became the East Persia Cordon against German infiltration toward Afghanistan; from March 1916 it was the Seistan Force (Dyer from Feb 1916), later extended to Meshed and the Transcaspian line.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Seistan Force' (cross-check; formation July 1915, Seistan Force from March 1916, last elements out Nov 1920)
Despatch from India, March 1919 (longlongtrail.co.uk transcription) on the East Persia Cordon / Field Force

events.title: Tangestani attack on the British Residency at Bushehr
events.summary: Rais Ali Delvari and the Tangestanis, encouraged by the German agent Wassmuss, attacked the Residency on 12 July 1915; the British occupied Bushehr on 8 Aug.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Rais-Ali Delvari' and 'British occupation of Bushehr' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: British occupation of Bushehr
events.summary: British troops took over Bushehr's government on 8 Aug 1915, disarming the gendarmerie; the occupation ended by agreement on 16 Oct 1915, and Persian postal authorities resumed on 18 Oct.
sources: Wikipedia, 'British occupation of Bushehr' (8 Aug - 16 Oct 1915; cross-check)

events.title: Kuchek Khan's Jangalis take to the forests of Gilan
events.summary: Mirza Kuchek Khan began the Jangali movement in October 1915 to free Gilan of the Russian army; it later controlled much of Gilan's administration (1917) and survived until December 1921.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Jangali movement' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/jangali-movement/)

events.title: Nationalist government at Kermanshah
events.summary: Nationalists who had left Tehran formed a Committee/National Government at Qom and then Kermanshah (Nezam al-Saltaneh Mafi) allied with the Central Powers; it was driven out by the Russian entry into Kermanshah on 26 Feb 1916, returned with the Ottomans in July 1916 and collapsed in March 1917.
sources: University of Edinburgh thesis abstract, 'Muhajirat and the National Government of Kermanshah, 1915-1917' (era.ed.ac.uk) [search extract]
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Kermanshah iv. History to 1953' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kermanshah-04-history-to-1953/)

events.title: Baratov's Russian expedition takes Hamadan and Kermanshah
events.summary: The Russian Caucasian Cavalry Corps landed at Anzali (Oct 1915), took Hamadan in December 1915 (3 or 15 Dec) and entered Kermanshah on 26 Feb 1916, then Sanandaj and Bijar on 1-3 March and Qasr-e Shirin in May.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Kermanshah operation' (cross-check; Russian entry to Kermanshah 26 Feb 1916)
Wikipedia, 'Persian campaign (World War I)' (cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations)

events.title: South Persia Rifles raised and disbanded
events.summary: Sir Percy Sykes landed at Bandar Abbas in March 1916 to raise a British-officered force of up to 11,000 men; brigades sat at Shiraz, Kerman and Bandar Abbas by December 1916; the force was disbanded in 1921 and some personnel entered the new Iranian army.
sources: Wikipedia, 'South Persia Rifles' (cross-check; raised 1916, disbanded 1921)

events.title: Ottoman XIII Corps retakes Kermanshah and Hamadan
events.summary: Ali Ihsan's XIII Corps took Kermanshah on 2 July and Hamadan on 10 Aug 1916, forcing Baratov north; the Ottomans held Kermanshah until the retreat after Baghdad's fall (March 1917).
sources: Wikipedia, 'Persian campaign (World War I)' (cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations)
Wikipedia, 'Kermanshah operation' (cross-check; Russian entry to Kermanshah 26 Feb 1916)

events.title: Russian troops evacuate Persia
events.summary: After the Bolshevik revolution most Russian troops left Persia between January and March 1918; the last Russians left Tabriz on 28 Feb 1918, while a few under Baratov entered British service.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Russia i. Russo-Iranian Relations up to the Bolshevik Revolution' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/russia-i-relations/)
Wikipedia, 'Russian occupation of Tabriz' (cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915)

events.title: Dunsterforce enters Persia
events.summary: Maj.-Gen. Dunsterville's advance party reached Hamadan in Feb 1918; Dunsterforce held the road from Mesopotamia to Anzali, fought at Manjil (Aug 1918), held Baku 18 Aug-14 Sept and was disbanded on 17 Sept 1918 when Norperforce took over.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Dunsterforce' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Jangali movement' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/jangali-movement/)

events.title: Ottoman reoccupation of Tabriz, Salmas and Urmia
events.summary: Ottoman IV Corps entered Tabriz on 8 June 1918 (another date: 18 June), took Dilman (Salmas) on 18 June and Urmia on 31 July 1918; they withdrew after the Armistice of Mudros (30 Oct 1918).
sources: Wikipedia, 'Persian campaign (World War I)' (cross-check; Ottoman and Russian dated operations)
Wikipedia, 'Russian occupation of Tabriz' (cross-check; 30 Apr 1909 - 28 Feb 1918, break 17 Dec 1914 - 31 Jan 1915)

events.title: Norperforce formed
events.summary: The British North Persia Force (HQ Qazvin; main body at Manjil; a battalion at Zanjan) was formed on 16 Sept 1918 with about 6,000 men to hold the Hamadan-Qazvin-Anzali route.
sources: FIBIS wiki, 'Norperforce' (wiki.fibis.org/w/Norperforce)

events.title: Khiabani's rising in Tabriz
events.summary: Armed supporters of Sheikh Mohammad Khiabani gathered on 7 April 1920, the Swedish-officered police left and the Democrats proclaimed Azadistan; the bazaar closed in support on 9 April.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Ḵiābāni, Shaikh Moḥammad' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/%E1%B8%B5iabani-shaikh-mo%E1%B8%A5ammad/)

events.title: Soviet landing at Anzali and proclamation of the Soviet Republic of Gilan
events.summary: The Red Army landed at Anzali on 18 May 1920; Kuchek Khan's Jangalis welcomed it and the Soviet Republic of Gilan was proclaimed at Rasht on 4-6 June 1920 (Iranica: 5-6 June; Wikipedia: 4 June).
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Jangali movement' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/jangali-movement/)
Wikipedia, 'Persian Socialist Soviet Republic' (cross-check; Red Army withdrawal 8 Sept 1921)

events.title: Khiabani's movement crushed
events.summary: Cossack forces entered Tabriz on 14 Sept 1920 and Khiabani was found and killed.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Ḵiābāni, Shaikh Moḥammad' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/%E1%B8%B5iabani-shaikh-mo%E1%B8%A5ammad/)

events.title: Last British elements leave eastern Persia
events.summary: The last elements of the Seistan Force/East Persia Cordon withdrew from Persia in November 1920; British troops remained at Khash in Sarhad until 1 March 1924.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Seistan Force' (cross-check; formation July 1915, Seistan Force from March 1916, last elements out Nov 1920)
Koyagi, M., 'Tribes and Smugglers in Iran's Eastern Borderlands, 1921-41', Iranian Studies (Cambridge UP, 2021), pp. 405-422

events.title: Reza Khan's Luristan campaigns
events.summary: The army deployed to Luristan in April 1921, took Borujerd (Oct 1923) and Khorramabad (Nov 1923), faced a revolt in May 1924, fought its last major engagement in 1926 and, per Wikipedia, had direct control by 1928; Iranica says the war lasted to 1933 although migration was banned from 1929.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Luri tribal insurgency in Pahlavi Iran' (cross-check; Reza Khan's Luristan campaigns 1921-33)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Luristan' articles (iranicaonline.org), search extract: army in Luristan 1922, war to 1933, migration banned from 1929

events.title: Norperforce completely withdrawn
events.summary: On 21 April 1921 Norperforce was withdrawn into Mesopotamia, leaving its small arms, artillery and transport to the Persian Cossacks.
sources: FIBIS wiki, 'Norperforce' (wiki.fibis.org/w/Norperforce)

events.title: Red Army leaves Gilan; Reza Khan's forces take Rasht
events.summary: After the Persian-Soviet treaty of 26 Feb 1921 the Red Army left Gilan on 8 Sept 1921 and Reza Khan's army seized the province in October; Kuchek Khan died in December 1921.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Persian Socialist Soviet Republic' (cross-check; Red Army withdrawal 8 Sept 1921)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Jangali movement' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/jangali-movement/)

events.title: Col. Pesyan killed; Khorasan returns to Tehran
events.summary: Pesyan died fighting Kurdish forces under Sardar Mo'azzaz Bojnurdi, acting for Qavam al-Saltaneh, near Quchan on 3 Oct 1921; the Gendarmerie regime in Khorasan collapsed.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Pesyan, Mohammad Taqi Khan' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/pesyan-mohammad-taqi-khan/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Lahuti's gendarmerie revolt at Tabriz (duration unverified)
events.summary: Maj. Abolqasem Lahuti staged a revolt at Tabriz in 1922 and fled to the USSR after its failure. I could not verify its date or whether it held the city for more than about a week, so no region record is made.
sources: Not independently verified in this research pass; reconstructed from general scholarship

events.title: Simko defeated and flees to Iraq
events.summary: Reza Khan's army (about 10,000) defeated Simko in summer 1922 and took Chehriq; Simko fled across the frontier. He returned under pardon, rebelled again in 1926 and was killed at Ushnu on 30 June 1930. Month of the 1922 defeat varies in sources.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Simko Shikak revolt (1918-1922)' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Čahrīq' (iranicaonline.org) and 'Khiābāni'/'Great Britain v' extracts on Simko 1920-22 [search extracts]

events.title: Shahsevan pacified and disarmed
events.summary: Iranica: in winter and spring 1922-23 the Shahsevan were among the first major tribal groups pacified and disarmed by Reza Khan's army.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Shahsevan' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/shahsevan/)

events.title: British hand Khash to Iran
events.summary: A ceremony on 1 March 1924 ended the British occupation of Iranian Baluchistan: Salar Amjad thanked the British and the Union Jack at Khash was replaced by the Iranian flag.
sources: Koyagi, M., 'Tribes and Smugglers in Iran's Eastern Borderlands, 1921-41', Iranian Studies (Cambridge UP, 2021), pp. 405-422

events.title: Reza Khan ends Sheikh Khaz'al's rule
events.summary: Reza Khan mobilised about 15,000 troops around Khuzestan; Khaz'al submitted at Ahvaz on 6 Dec 1924, was pardoned on 19 Dec and was seized on his yacht on 18 April 1925.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Ḵazʿal Khan' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/kazal-khan/)

events.title: Army disarms the Turkmen of the Gorgan plain
events.summary: In 1925 army contingents were sent to establish order and disarm the Turkmen tribes, and some were forced to settle at Gonbad-e Qabus.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Gorgān vii. History from the Safavids to the end of the Pahlavi era' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/gorgan-vii/)

events.title: Bojnurd bombed; end of the Kurdish ilkhani system in Khorasan
events.summary: Reza Khan's army bombed Bojnurd on 18 May 1925, the turning point in the destruction of the Shadlu/Za'faranlu ilkhanis; forced settlement followed from 1929.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xvii. The Kurdish Communities of Khorasan' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xvii-the-kurdish-communities-of-khorasan/)

events.title: Jahanbani's Baluchistan campaign
events.summary: Gen. Amanollah Jahanbani's army defeated Dost Mohammad Khan Baluch in the winter of 1928-29; he was pardoned on condition of living in Tehran, escaped and was hanged for murder on 16 Jan 1930.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Baluchistan i. Geography, History and Ethnography' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/baluchistan-index/baluchistan-i/) [search extract]
Wikipedia, 'Dost Mohammad Khan Baloch' (cross-check)
Koyagi, M., 'Tribes and Smugglers in Iran's Eastern Borderlands, 1921-41', Iranian Studies (Cambridge UP, 2021), pp. 405-422

events.title: End of the walis of Pusht-e Kuh
events.summary: Iranica: the quasi-autonomous walis of Pusht-e Kuh ruled "until about 1929", after which migration of the tribes was banned.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Pošt-e Kuh' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/post-e-kuh/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Luristan' articles (iranicaonline.org), search extract: army in Luristan 1922, war to 1933, migration banned from 1929

events.title: Southern tribal rising of 1929
events.summary: In early spring 1929 the Qashqai rose and by June had Shiraz under siege and most of Fars outside the city in rebel hands; Boir Ahmad, Khamseh and Bakhtiari groups joined. The government agreed amnesty terms in August 1929.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Persian tribal uprisings of 1929' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: Tang-e Tamradi: Boir Ahmad and Mamasani defeat the army
events.summary: In August 1930 the Boir Ahmad coalition with Mamasani chief Emamqoli Khan inflicted heavy losses (about 400 soldiers killed) on Reza Shah's advancing army at Tang-e Tamradi.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Boir Aḥmadī' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/boir-ahmadi/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: Boir Ahmad khans executed; military government
events.summary: The Boir Ahmad khans surrendered and were executed in 1932; a local military government then imposed order for about a decade.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Boir Aḥmadī' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/boir-ahmadi/)

events.title: Qashqai revolt of 1932 and death of Soulat al-Dowleh
events.summary: The Qashqai rebelled in 1932, Soulat al-Dowleh was arrested and killed in 1933, and the Shah's mechanised army cut migration routes.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qašqāʾi tribal confederacy i. History' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasqai-tribal-confederacy-i/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: Bakhtiari khans detribalised
events.summary: Ilkhani and ilbegi titles were abolished in 1933, several khans were arrested and some executed in 1934 and the tribal territory was divided between Isfahan and Khuzestan in 1936.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Baḵtīārī' articles incl. 'Baḵtīārī tribe', 'Esfandīār Khan', 'Baktiari ii' (iranicaonline.org) [search extracts]

events.title: British abandon Henjam at Reza Shah's request
events.summary: The British coaling station and naval base at Henjam was abandoned in 1935 at the request of Reza Shah, operations moving to Bahrain.
sources: Qatar Digital Library, 'British Naval Bases in the Gulf, 1820-1935: A History of Tensions' (qdl.qa) [search extract]

events.title: Anglo-Soviet invasion and occupation of Iran
events.summary: British and Soviet forces invaded on 25 Aug 1941: the Soviets took Azerbaijan, Gilan, Mazandaran, Gorgan and Khorasan, the British Khuzestan and the road to Hamadan. Both entered Tehran on 17 Sept 1941 and withdrew to their zones by 17 Oct; Iranian administration continued. The Tripartite Treaty (29 Jan 1942) declared the troops were not an occupation and required withdrawal within six months of the war's end.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)

events.title: Reza Shah abdicates; tribes recover autonomy
events.summary: After the abdication on 16 Sept 1941 the Qashqai brothers returned to Fars, the Boir Ahmad tribal system "rebounded with amazing vigor" and Kurdish leaders in the Soviet zone rearmed; general accounts also have Lur and Bakhtiari nomadism returning, which is not documented in detail here.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qašqāʾi tribal confederacy i. History' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasqai-tribal-confederacy-i/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Boir Aḥmadī' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/boir-ahmadi/)
Wikipedia, 'Republic of Mahabad' (cross-check)

events.title: Soviet troops leave Khorasan
events.summary: Iranica says Soviet troops occupied all of Khorasan "until the winter of 1943"; the other Soviet-occupied provinces were held until 1946.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Khorasan xi. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/khorasan-xi-history-in-the-qajar-and-pahlavi-periods/)

events.title: Democrats seize Tabriz; Azerbaijan Autonomous Government proclaimed
events.summary: The Democratic Party of Azerbaijan, protected by Soviet troops that blocked the Iranian army, took power in Tabriz around 20-21 Nov 1945 and proclaimed the Autonomous Government of Azerbaijan under Ja'far Pishevari on 12 Dec 1945.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)
Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)

events.title: Republic of Mahabad proclaimed
events.summary: The Kurdistan Republic under Qazi Muhammad was proclaimed at Mahabad on 22 Jan 1946, covering Mahabad, Bukan, Naghadeh, Piranshahr and Oshnavieh.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Republic of Mahabad' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)

events.title: British (and US) troops leave Iran
events.summary: British and American forces left Iran by the 2 March 1946 deadline of the Tripartite Treaty (British began withdrawing in January).
sources: Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)
Wikipedia, 'Anglo-Soviet invasion of Iran' (cross-check)

events.title: Soviet troops leave northern Iran
events.summary: The Soviets missed the 2 March deadline; after pressure (UNSC) and the Qavam-Soviet agreement of 4 April they announced withdrawal on 24 March and were gone by about 6-9 May 1946.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)

events.title: Southern tribes' revolt against the Qavam government
events.summary: In September 1946 the Qashqai-led "National Movement of the South" rose, seizing Kazerun and Abadeh and threatening Shiraz until the Tudeh ministers were dismissed in October.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qašqāʾi tribal confederacy i. History' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasqai-tribal-confederacy-i/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: Iranian army enters Tabriz
events.summary: Iranian forces began advancing on 9 Dec 1946 and entered Tabriz on 12-13 Dec as Pishevari fled to Baku, ending the Azerbaijan People's Government.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Azarbaijan v. History from 1941 to 1947' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/azerbaijan-v/)
Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)

events.title: Iranian army enters Mahabad
events.summary: Isolated after the Soviet withdrawal and the fall of Tabriz, Mahabad was entered by the Iranian army on 15-17 Dec 1946, ending the republic.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Iran crisis of 1946' (cross-check)
Wikipedia, 'Republic of Mahabad' (cross-check)

events.title: Qashqai Four Brothers exiled
events.summary: After supporting Mosaddeq the four Qashqai brothers were exiled and their property confiscated in 1954; the confederacy's autonomy ended, and in 1963 the government declared tribes non-existent.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qašqāʾi tribal confederacy i. History' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasqai-tribal-confederacy-i/)

events.title: Boir Ahmad khans' revolt against land reform
events.summary: In 1962-63 two Boir Ahmad khans resisted land division, ambushed a column in the Gachina/Gochestan pass and were crushed in June 1963; leaders were executed. The revolt did not hold ground for a month and is not mapped separately.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Boir Aḥmadī' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/boir-ahmadi/)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Fārs iv. History in the Qajar and Pahlavi Periods' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/fars-iv/)

events.title: Islamic Revolution
events.summary: The fall of the monarchy on 11 Feb 1979 collapsed state authority in several peripheral regions for weeks to months.
sources: Wikipedia, '1979 Iranian ethnic unrest' (cross-check)

events.title: Kurdish groups seize garrisons in Sanandaj, Paveh, Saqqez, Marivan and Mahabad
events.summary: In mid-March 1979 Kurdish factions took the police headquarters and army bases in Sanandaj (17-19 March), Paveh, Saqqez and Marivan; Mahabad was in Kurdish hands from early March.
sources: Wikipedia, '1979 Kurdish rebellion in Iran' (cross-check)

events.title: Khomeini's jihad: Iranian offensive retakes Kurdish towns
events.summary: After Khomeini's jihad declaration on 17 Aug 1979 the army took Sanandaj and Saqqez (by 1 Sept), Mahabad (3 Sept) and Sardasht, Bukan and Piranshahr (4-6 Sept). The KDPI retook Mahabad on 20 Oct 1979.
sources: Wikipedia, '1979 Kurdish rebellion in Iran' (cross-check)
Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qāsemlu, ʿAbd-al-Raḥmān' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasemlu/)

events.title: Qashqai insurgency of Khosrow Khan
events.summary: After an attempt to arrest Khosrow Khan in June 1980 the Qashqai insurgents defied the government for two years until a Revolutionary Guards night attack in April 1982; Khosrow Khan was hanged on 8 Oct 1982 and Nasser Khan died in 1984.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qašqāʾi tribal confederacy i. History' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasqai-tribal-confederacy-i/)

events.title: Iraq invades Iran
events.summary: Iraq attacked on 22 Sept 1980 across a 400-mile front, taking Qasr-e Shirin, Mehran and a salient in Khuzestan; by December 1980 only parts of Khuzestan were occupied.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Iraq vii. Iran-Iraq War' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/iraq-vii-iran-iraq-war/)
Wikipedia, 'Battle of Khorramshahr (1980)' and 'Battle of Khorramshahr (1982)' (cross-check)

events.title: Siege of Abadan lifted
events.summary: Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh broke the siege of Abadan that had begun in late 1980.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Iraq vii. Iran-Iraq War' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/iraq-vii-iran-iraq-war/)

events.title: Khorramshahr liberated
events.summary: Iranian forces retook Khorramshahr on 24 May 1982 (Operation Beit ol-Moqaddas, 24 April-24 May), after the city had fallen to Iraq on 24 Oct-10 Nov 1980.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Iraq vii. Iran-Iraq War' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/iraq-vii-iran-iraq-war/)
Wikipedia, 'Battle of Khorramshahr (1980)' and 'Battle of Khorramshahr (1982)' (cross-check)

events.title: Iraq announces withdrawal from Iranian territory
events.summary: Iraq announced on 20 June 1982 that it would withdraw to the international border; Iran then carried the war into Iraq.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Iraq vii. Iran-Iraq War' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/iraq-vii-iran-iraq-war/)

events.title: KDPI withdraws to Iraq
events.summary: After the Iranian counter-offensives of 1982-83 the KDPI withdrew into Iraqi territory by early 1984; sporadic Komala activity continued but no territory was held.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Qāsemlu, ʿAbd-al-Raḥmān' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/qasemlu/)
Wikipedia, '1979 Kurdish rebellion in Iran' (cross-check)

events.title: Post-1983: no area outside central control lasting a month (research note)
events.summary: After the KDPI left for Iraq (early 1984) and the Iran-Iraq war ended (1988/1990), I found no area of Iran outside the central government's control for as long as a month. Insurgencies (PJAK, Jundallah/Jaish al-Adl, People's Fighters Front) and the unrest of 2009, 2019 and 2022 did not hold territory. Exceptions flagged in the 2026 events: a few days in January 2026 (Abdanan, Malekshahi) and ongoing 2026 Kurdish-IRGC fighting where no confirmed territorial holding was reported. No region record is made for 1984-2026.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, '2026 Iran war' (britannica.com/event/2026-Iran-war), status as of 1 Oct 2026
Wikipedia, '2026 Kurdish rebellion in Iran' and 'Western Iran clashes (2026-present)' (cross-check; no confirmed territorial holdings)
Iran International, 6 Jan 2026 and i24NEWS, 7 Jan 2026 (protesters in Abdanan/Malekshahi) [search extracts]; JISS, 'Iran After the January 2026 Protests'

events.title: Iraq retakes Mehran; Iran regains it (Karbala-1)
events.summary: Iraq's II Corps captured Mehran on 15-19 May 1986 and Iran recaptured the area in Operation Karbala-1 (30 June-3 July), defeating a Republican Guard counter-attack on 4 July.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Battle of Mehran (1986)' (cross-check)

events.title: Operation Forty Stars and the MEK's Eternal Light
events.summary: On 18 June 1988 Iraqi forces and the MEK captured Mehran; on 12 July Iraq entered Dehloran, Qasr-e Shirin, Sumar, Naft Shahr and Sar-e Pol-e Zahab and withdrew from the towns after Iran accepted the ceasefire. On 26 July the MEK's Eternal Light (Forough-e Javidan) reached Eslamabad-e Gharb and was defeated in Operation Mersad within days; none of these gains lasted a month except possibly Mehran (low confidence).
sources: Wikipedia, 'Operation Forty Stars' and 'Operation Mersad' (cross-check; dates of Mehran 1988 uncertain)
Wikipedia, 'Tawakalna ala Allah Operations' (cross-check; Iraqi entry to Dehloran/Qasr-e Shirin 12 July 1988)

events.title: UN ceasefire takes effect
events.summary: The ceasefire under UN Security Council Resolution 598 took effect on 20 Aug 1988; UNIIMOG monitored until February 1991, while Iraq kept hold of some Iranian border land.
sources: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Iraq vii. Iran-Iraq War' (https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/iraq-vii-iran-iraq-war/)
Reports of the UN Secretary-General on UNIIMOG (Sept 1990) and contemporary press (CS Monitor 17 Aug 1990; UPI 16 Aug 1990) [search extracts]

events.title: Iraq withdraws from the last occupied Iranian territory
events.summary: On 15-16 Aug 1990 Saddam Hussein accepted the 1975 Algiers border and offered to withdraw from about 2,600 km2 of Iranian territory; almost all forces were back across the border within about five days and the UN reported the withdrawal almost complete on 24 Sept 1990.
sources: Reports of the UN Secretary-General on UNIIMOG (Sept 1990) and contemporary press (CS Monitor 17 Aug 1990; UPI 16 Aug 1990) [search extracts]

events.title: Abdanan and Malekshahi briefly outside government control
events.summary: During the Dec 2025-Jan 2026 protests security forces withdrew from Abdanan and Malekshahi (Ilam) for a few days around 6-8 January 2026 and protesters took the towns; the sources found do not give the date of restored control. Under the one-month threshold, so no region record.
sources: Iran International, 6 Jan 2026 and i24NEWS, 7 Jan 2026 (protesters in Abdanan/Malekshahi) [search extracts]; JISS, 'Iran After the January 2026 Protests'

events.title: 2026 Iran war (US-Israeli strikes): no Iranian territory seized
events.summary: The war that began on 28 Feb 2026 saw strikes on Kharg, Qeshm, Larak, Kish and Abu Musa and an Israeli special-forces ground raid on 2 March, but Britannica reports that no Iranian territory was seized as of 1 Oct 2026; a ceasefire in April and an MOU on 17 June 2026 collapsed on 6-7 July.
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, '2026 Iran war' (britannica.com/event/2026-Iran-war), status as of 1 Oct 2026

events.title: PJAK/KDPI-IRGC fighting in Iranian Kurdistan (ongoing)
events.summary: Armed clashes since 7 June 2026 around Marivan, Mahabad, Piranshahr, Baneh and Saqqez involve mobile operations rather than held territory according to the sources found; flagged for review if later reporting shows held areas.
sources: Wikipedia, '2026 Kurdish rebellion in Iran' and 'Western Iran clashes (2026-present)' (cross-check; no confirmed territorial holdings)
